title: Exact sum base change is the mate of the inverse pullback square
statement: Let A be a commutative ring and let e:U→X and e′:U′→X′ be etale morphisms in a Cartesian square with vertical arrows w′:U′→U and w:X′→X [def-weil-pbc-cartesian-square]. On ordinary unbounded derived categories of A-module sheaves [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories], use the sum-extension/inverse-image adjunctions [def-weil-pbc-etale-sum-extension] [lem-amb-etale-adjoint-locality] obtained by localizing their complex adjunctions. The mate [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-mate] of mapDerivedCategoryEtaleLowerShriekBaseChangeIso.hom is exactly the inverse exact pullback-square comparison [def-kun-unbounded-exchange], with the canonical exact inverse-image composition maps [def-pur-etale-exact-pullback-unit-composition-comparisons]. No Noetherian, finiteness or boundedness hypotheses are required.

source.place: Tag 03S6; exact localization of the ordinary sum base-change unit equation

proof.text: The ordinary sum base-change unit equation unit_map_etaleLowerShriekSquareBaseChangeMap_app identifies the mate of the ordinary sum exchange with the inverse ordinary pullback square. Apply the inverse mate equivalence and its unit formula, then take its counit transpose. The private mate_eq_of_unit helper proves the uniqueness by an adjunction hom-bijection.

Write both sides of that counit equation as finite expressions in six exact functors: the two sum functors, their two inverse-image right adjoints and the two vertical inverse images. The cells are the square comparison, the sum base-change comparison and the two counits. Apply exact_derived_transformation_pasting to descend the equality. Its cell formula identifies the two isomorphism cells with the specified exact derived comparisons. Localization of the complex adjunction identifies the counit cells with the specified onDerivedCategory counits; this equality follows on complexes by localization natural-transformation extensionality and the derived composition factors.

Evaluate the descended equality at an arbitrary unbounded K. Under the second specified derived adjunction, it is exactly the equality of the transposes of the mate of the sum exchange and the inverse exact pullback-square map. The counit formula for mateEquiv and injectivity of the hom-bijection prove the result. The argument also covers identity maps and empty sites, without any coefficient nontriviality assumption.

lean.statement:
theorem etaleExactSumBaseChangeMate
    (A : Type (u + 1)) [CommRing A]
    {U U' X X' : Scheme.{u}} {e : U ⟶ X} {e' : U' ⟶ X'}
    {w : X' ⟶ X} {w' : U' ⟶ U} [Etale e] [Etale e']
    (sq : IsPullback w' e' e w) :
    (mateEquiv
      (derivedEtaleLowerShriekUpperStarAdjunction (ModuleCat.{u + 1} A) e inferInstance)
      (derivedEtaleLowerShriekUpperStarAdjunction (ModuleCat.{u + 1} A) e' inferInstance)
      (TwoSquare.mk _ _ _ _
        (mapDerivedCategoryEtaleLowerShriekBaseChangeIso (ModuleCat.{u + 1} A) sq).hom)
      ).natTrans =
      (exactDerivedSquareUpperStarIso (ModuleCat.{u + 1} A) sq.toCommSq).inv
